Clap, Catch, Connect! 👏🎯

In this engaging activity, the child claps in rhythm every time the teacher catches the ball. It may look simple, but it’s doing powerful work in the brain!

✨ Visual Attention – The child has to closely watch the ball and the teacher’s actions, strengthening focus and tracking skills.

✨ Memory – Remembering when to clap and maintaining the rhythm builds working memory and sequencing abilities.

✨ Emotional Regulation – Following a predictable rhythm helps the child stay calm, organised, and in control of their responses.

✨ Coordination & Timing – Matching the clap with the catch improves timing, motor planning, and body coordination.

🧠 What does the “Integration Clap” do in the brain?
The integration clap activates communication between the left and right hemispheres of the brain. This cross-hemispheric coordination strengthens neural pathways responsible for attention, processing speed, and self-regulation. It helps the brain work as a more connected and efficient system, which is essential for learning.

Activities like these show how play-based learning can build strong cognitive foundations while keeping children engaged and joyful 💛

Phonics C2C Training🔡🎊

We are currently conducting an ongoing Phonics C2C training session at one of our centers for one of our trainees. This hands-on training is designed to equip educators with practical strategies, structured techniques, and a deep understanding of phonics instruction.

Through this program, our trainee is learning how to:✨ Build strong letter-sound relationships✨ Deliver engaging, multisensory phonics sessions✨ Support early readers with confidence and clarity✨ Use structured methods to enhance reading and spelling skills

The Phonics C2C program focuses not just on theory, but on real classroom application—ensuring that every trainee feels confident to implement what they learn with children.
